label: NOTE: what this set covers, and what it cannot
why: V90SpectralShaper.cpp's constructor and destructor.  What cannot be mutated into a caught failure is the SYNTAX of the +0x38 store: moving it from the member-initialiser list into the body changes the instruction order and nothing an observer can see, because the encoder's constructor does not read +0x38.  That is a codegen claim (finding F1243) and it is checked by the similarity tier, not here.  The two buffers' element type is likewise not mutable HERE -- `unsigned short *` against `short *` allocates the same 48 bytes and neither of these two members dereferences either pointer.  It is settled all the same, by the two callees that take them as `const short *` (finding F5850), and t_v90spectrellis.cpp's trials are where a wrong element type would show.  The rest of the file's members carry their own suites; this set is the two that were written first.
